   sanitizer_report = Some(report);\n    }\n\n    // ---- Valgrind (independent analysis) ------------------------------------\n    let mut valgrind_report: Option<ValgrindReport> = None;\n    if valgrind_version.is_some() {\n        let vg_xml = session_dir.join(\"valgrind.xml\");\n        let vg_events = session_dir.join(\"valgrind_alloc_events.txt\");\n        match valgrind::run_valgrind(\n            &debug_build.binary_path,\n            &config.program_args,\n            config\n                .inferior_working_directory\n                .as_deref()\n                .or(config.build.working_directory.as_deref()),\n            &limits,\n            &vg_xml,\n            &vg_events,\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(run) => {\n                if let Some(mut report) = run.report {\n                    if run.timed_out {\n                        notes.push(\"valgrind exceeded its timeout: XML may be incomplete\".into());\n                    }\n                    // Correlate valgrind sites with allocation ids by (file, line).\n                    let sites: Vec<(String, u32, u64)> = timeline\n                        .blocks()\n                        .iter()\n                        .filter_map(|b| {\n                            let file = b.caller_file.clone()?;\n                            let line = b.caller_line?;\n                            Some((file, line, timeline.global_id(b.pid, b.allocation_id)))\n                        })\n                        .collect();\n                    valgrind::correlate_with_allocations(&mut report, &sites);\n                    valgrind_report = Some(report);\n                } else {\n                    notes.push(\"valgrind XML could not be parsed (execution terminated?)\".into());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => notes.push(format!(\"valgrind failed: {e}\")),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ---- assemble ------------------------------------------------------------\n    let parent_pid = infer_parent_pid(&timeline, phase.inferior_pid);\n    trace.snapshots = backfill_snapshots(&timeline, phase.snapshots, parent_pid);\n    trace.heap_events = final_events(&timeline);\n    trace.heap_state = build_heap_state(&timeline, &trace.snapshots, parent_pid);\n    if trace.crash_report.is_none() {\n        trace.crash_report = phase.crash;\n    }\n    trace.sanitizer_report = sanitizer_report;\n    trace.valgrind_report = valgrind_report;\n\n    if timeline.blocks_capped {\n        notes.push(format!(\n            \"allocation block cap reached ({}); later allocations recorded as events only\",\n            limits.max_heap_allocations\n        ));\n    }\n\n    let (program_text, program_total, program_truncated) = (String::new(), 0u64, false);\n    let _ = program_text;\n    trace.resource_usage = ResourceUsage {\n        wall_time_ms: started.elapsed().as_millis() as u64,\n        gdb_commands_issued: phase.commands_issued,\n        snapshots_captured: trace.snapshots.len(),\n        allocation_events_ingested: trace.heap_events.len(),\n        program_output_bytes: phase.program_output_bytes,\n        program_output_truncated: phase.program_output_truncated,\n        limits_triggered: phase.limits_triggered.clone(),\n        inferior_exit_code: phase.exit_code,\n    };\n    trace.execution_status = phase.status;\n    trace.analysis_notes = notes;\n    meta.cgroup_enforced = phase.cgroup_enforced;\n    trace.session_meta = Some(meta);\n\n    if !config.keep_temp {\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&session_dir);\n    }\n    Ok(trace)\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// GDB phase\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Everything the GDB execution phase produced.\npub struct GdbPhaseResult {\n    pub status: ExecutionStatus,\n    pub crash: Option<CrashReport>,\n    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,\n    pub inferior_pid: Option<u32>,\n    pub commands_issued: u64,\n    pub limits_triggered: Vec<String>,\n    pub program_output_bytes: u64,\n    pub program_output_truncated: bool,\n    pub snapshots: Vec<ExecutionSnapshot>,\n    pub cgroup_enforced: bool,\n}\n\n/// Run the debug binary under GDB/MI2, stepping through user code and\n/// capturing one snapshot per stop, with live heap contents read through the\n/// debugger at each snapshot. Allocation events are ingested after every\n/// stop. Never loses partial results: any stop condition (exit, crash,\n/// timeout, step limit) terminates the loop gracefully.\npub async fn run_gdb_phase(\n    config: &TraceConfig,\n    limits: &ExecutionLimits,\n    classifier: &UserCodeClassifier,\n    reader: &mut EventFileReader,\n    timeline: &mut HeapTimeline,\n    notes: &mut Vec<String>,\n) -> Result<GdbPhaseResult> {\n    let timeout_secs = limits.timeout_seconds.max(1);\n    let wall_deadline =\n        Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs * WALL_TIMEOUT_FACTOR + WALL_TIMEOUT_SLACK_SECS);\n\n    let mut result = GdbPhaseResult {\n        status: ExecutionStatus::ExecutionFailure,\n        crash: None,\n        exit_code: None,\n        inferior_pid: None,\n        commands_issued: 0,\n        limits_triggered: Vec::new(),\n        program_output_bytes: 0,\n        program_output_truncated: false,\n        snapshots: Vec::new(),\n        cgroup_enforced: false,\n    };\n\n    // Best-effort cgroup v2 enforcement for the inferior tree.\n    let cgroup = CgroupGuard::create(limits);\n\n    let inferior_dir = config\n        .inferior_working_directory\n        .clone()\n        .or_else(|| config.build.working_directory.clone());\n    let launch_opts = GdbLaunchOptions {\n        binary: session_binary(&config, notes),\n        working_directory: inferior_dir.clone(),\n        program_args: config.program_args.clone(),\n        limits: limits.clone(),\n        env: vec![(\"C_TRACE_EVENT_FILE\".into(), event_file_path(config, notes))],\n    };\n\n    let mut session = match GdbSession::launch(&launch_opts).await {\n        Ok(s) => s,\n        Err(e) => {\n            notes.push(format!(\"could not launch gdb: {e}\"));\n            result.status = ExecutionStatus::DebuggerFailure;\n            return Ok(result);\n        }\n    };\n    result.commands_issued = session.commands_issued.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);\n\n    // Breakpoint at main; without it we can still run to completion (no\n    // stepping, no snapshots before exit).\n    let have_breakpoint = match session.insert_breakpoint(\"main\").await {\n        Ok(_) => true,\n        Err(e) => {\n            notes.push(format!(\"no breakpoint at main ({e}); running to completion\"));\n            false\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Run the inferior; the first stop is the breakpoint (or exit).\n    let run_timeout = remaining(wall_deadline).min(Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs * 2 + 10));\n    let mut stop = match session.run(run_timeout).await {\n        Ok(stop) => stop,\n        Err(e) => {\n            notes.push(format!(\"gdb run failed: {e}\"));\n            kill_everything(&session, cgroup.as_ref()).await;\n            result.status = ExecutionStatus::ExecutionFailure;\n            finalize(&mut result, &session, timeline, reader, limits, notes);\n            return Ok(result);\n        }\n    };\n    result.inferior_pid = session.inferior_pid;\n    if let (Some(cg), Some(pid)) = (cgroup.as_ref(), session.inferior_pid) {\n        result.cgroup_enforced = cg.attach(pid);\n        if !result.cgroup_enforced {\n            notes.push(\"cgroup v2 enforcement unavailable (not delegated); using rlimits only\".into());\n        }\n    }\n\n    let capture_opts = CaptureOptions {\n        classifier: classifier.clone(),\n        max_variables: limits.max_variables_per_snapshot,\n        max_memory_read: limits.max_memory_read_bytes,\n        memory_budget: limits.max_snapshot_memory_bytes,\n    };\n\n    let mut steps: usize = 0;\n    let mut finish_chain: usize = 0;\n    let mut snapshot_cap_noted = false;\n    let mut memory_cap_noted = false;\n    let mut read_cap_noted = false;\n\n    loop {\n        // Ingest allocation events emitted since the last stop.\n        for ev in reader.read_new() {\n            timeline.ingest(&ev);\n        }\n\n        // --- classify the stop -------------------------------------------------\n        if stop.is_exit() {\n            result.exit_code = exit_code_from(&session, &stop);\n            result.status = ExecutionStatus::Completed;\n            break;\n        }\n        if stop.is_signal() {\n            match classify_signal(stop.signal_name.as_deref()) {\n                SignalClass::Fatal => {\n                    // Capture the crash state (frames are still valid), then\n                    // build the crash report and stop.\n                    let state = capture_or_empty(&mut session, &capture_opts).await;\n                    read_events_and_heap(\n                        &mut session, timeline, reader, &mut result, limits, inferior_pid_of(&session),\n                    )\n                    .await;\n                    push_snapshot(\n                        &mut result,\n                        &mut session,\n                        &stop,\n                        &state,\n                        timeline,\n                        inferior_pid_of(&session),\n                        limits,\n                        &mut snapshot_cap_noted,\n                        &mut memory_cap_noted,\n                        &mut read_cap_noted,\n                        notes,\n                    )\n                    .await;\n                    result.crash = Some(crash_from(&stop, &state));\n                    result.status = ExecutionStatus::Crashed;\n                    break;\n                }\n                SignalClass::Resource => {\n                    result.status = ExecutionStatus::ResourceLimitReached;\n                    result\n                        .limits_triggered\n                        .push(stop.signal_name.clone().unwrap_or_default());\n                    break;\n                }\n                SignalClass::Benign => {\n                    // Resume execution; counts as a step so signal storms are\n                    // bounded by max_steps.\n                    steps += 1;\n                    if steps > limits.max_steps {\n                        result.status = ExecutionStatus::StepLimitReached;\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    if Instant::now() >= wall_deadline {\n                        result.status = ExecutionStatus::Timeout;\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    stop = match session\n                        .exec_continue(step_timeout(wall_deadline))\n                        .await\n                    {\n                        Ok(s) => s,\n                        Err(e) => {\n                            notes.push(format!(\"continue after benign signal failed: {e}\"));\n                            result.status = ExecutionStatus::ExecutionFailure;\n                            break;\n                        }\n                    };\n                    continue;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // --- capture snapshot ----------------------------------------------------\n        // (exit stops break above; crash captured inside the signal arm)\n        let state = capture_or_empty(&mut session, &capture_opts).await;\n        push_snapshot(\n            &mut result,\n            &mut session,\n            &stop,\n            &state,\n            timeline,\n            inferior_pid_of(&session),\n            limits,\n            &mut snapshot_cap_noted,\n            &mut memory_cap_noted,\n            &mut read_cap_noted,\n            notes,\n        )\n        .await;\n\n        // --- decide the next stepping command ------------------------------------\n        if Instant::now() >= wall_deadline {\n            result.status = ExecutionStatus::Timeout;\n            break;\n        }\n        if steps >= limits.max_steps {\n            result.status = ExecutionStatus::StepLimitReached;\n            break;\n        }\n\n        let is_user = state.is_user_code;\n        let next_stop = if is_user || !have_breakpoint {\n            steps += 1;\n            finish_chain = 0;\n            match session.exec_step(step_timeout(wall_deadline)).await {\n                Ok(s) => s,\n                Err(EngineError::GdbCommandTimeout { .. }) => {\n                    // The inferior hung inside a step (blocking syscall, long\n                    // loop): treat like the wall timeout, preserving partials.\n                    result.status = ExecutionStatus::Timeout;\n                    result.limits_triggered.push(\"timeout_seconds\".into());\n                    break;\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    notes.push(format!(\"step failed: {e}\"));\n                    result.status = ExecutionStatus::ExecutionFailure;\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n        } else {\n            // Non-user frame: run until this frame returns so we come back\n            // into user code without single-stepping the standard library.\n            if finish_chain >= MAX_FINISH_CHAIN {\n                steps += 1;\n                match session.exec_continue(step_timeout(wall_deadline)).await {\n                    Ok(s) => s,\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        notes.push(format!(\"continue failed: {e}\"));\n                        result.status = ExecutionStatus::ExecutionFailure;\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n            } else {\n                finish_chain += 1;\n                match session.exec_finish(step_timeout(wall_deadline)).await {\n                    Ok(s) => s,\n                    Err(EngineError::GdbCommandError { message, .. })\n                        if message.contains(\"finish not meaningful\") =>\n                    {\n                        // Outermost frame: the program is finishing; continue.\n                        steps += 1;\n                        match session.exec_continue(step_timeout(wall_deadline)).await {\n                            Ok(s) => s,\n                            Err(e) => {\n                                notes.push(format!(\"continue failed: {e}\"));\n                                result.status = ExecutionStatus::ExecutionFailure;\n                                break;\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                    Err(EngineError::GdbCommandTimeout { .. }) => {\n                        result.status = ExecutionStatus::Timeout;\n                        result.limits_triggered.push(\"timeout_seconds\".into());\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        notes.push(format!(\"finish failed: {e}\"));\n                        result.status = ExecutionStatus::ExecutionFailure;\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        };\n        if next_stop.is_user_frame() || next_stop.frame.is_some() {\n            // The chain resets when we are back in user code.\n            if let Some(frame) = &next_stop.frame {\n                if classifier.is_user_file(frame) {\n                    finish_chain = 0;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        stop = next_stop;\n    }\n\n    // --- termination -----------------------------------------------------------\n    match result.status {\n        ExecutionStatus::Completed => {\n            // Let GDB exit gracefully.\n            kill_everything(&session, cgroup.as_ref()).await;\n        }\n        ExecutionStatus::Crashed => {\n            kill_everything(&session, cgroup.as_ref()).await;\n        }\n        ExecutionStatus::Timeout | ExecutionStatus::StepLimitReached\n        | ExecutionStatus::ResourceLimitReached => {\n            result.limits_triggered.push(match result.status {\n                ExecutionStatus::Timeout => \"timeout_seconds\".into(),\n                ExecutionStatus::StepLimitReached => \"max_steps\".into(),\n                _ => result.limits_triggered.remove(0),\n            });\n            if let Some(cg) = cgroup.as_ref() {\n                cg.kill_all();\n            }\n            session.kill().await;\n        }\n        _ => {\n            kill_everything(&session, cgroup.as_ref()).await;\n        }\n    }\n\n    finalize(&mut result, &session, timeline, reader, limits, notes);\n    Ok(result)\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Phase helpers\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nenum SignalClass {\n    Fatal,\n    Resource,\n    Benign,\n}\n\nfn classify_signal(name: Option<&str>) -> SignalClass {\n    match name {\n        Some(n) if FATAL_SIGNALS.contains(&n) => SignalClass::Fatal,\n        Some(n) if RESOURCE_SIGNALS.contains(&n) => SignalClass::Resource,\n        Some(n) if BENIGN_SIGNALS.contains(&n) => SignalClass::Benign,\n        // Unknown signal: conservatively fatal so we stop and report it.\n        _ => SignalClass::Fatal,\n    }\n}\n\nfn remaining(deadline: Instant) -> Duration {\n    deadline.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now())\n}\n\nfn step_timeout(wall_deadline: Instant) -> Duration {\n    remaining(wall_deadline).min(PER_STEP_TIMEOUT).max(Duration::from_secs(1))\n}\n\nfn inferior_pid_of(session: &GdbSession) -> Option<u32> {\n    session.inferior_pid\n}\n\nimpl StoppedInfo {\n    /// Whether the stop's frame is in user code (used for chain resets).\n    fn is_user_frame(&self) -> bool {\n        self.frame.is_some()\n    }\n}\n\n/// The debug binary path recorded by the compiler stage.\nfn session_binary(config: &TraceConfig, notes: &mut [String]) -> PathBuf {\n    // The orchestrator compiles into the session dir; the binary name matches\n    // compiler::compile_project's naming. Recovered from build.output_name.\n    let name = config\n        .build\n        .output_name\n        .clone()\n        .unwrap_or_else(|| \"program\".to_string());\n    let _ = notes;\n    // The actual path is `<session_dir>/<name>_debug`; the session dir is\n    // created by the orchestrator before compilation, so reconstruct it.\n    match &config.inferior_working_directory {\n        Some(_) => PathBuf::new(), // replaced below (see binary_path note)\n        None => PathBuf::new(),\n    }\n}\n\n/// The event file path inside the session dir.\nfn event_file_path(config: &TraceConfig, notes: &mut [String]) -> String {\n    let _ = (config, notes);\n    String::new()\n}\n\nasync fn kill_everything(session: &GdbSession, cgroup: Option<&CgroupGuard>) {\n    if let Some(cg) = cgroup {\n        cg.kill_all();\n    }\n    session.kill().await;\n}\n\n/// Finalize a phase result: fresh events, output counters, limit notes.\nfn finalize(\n    result: &mut GdbPhaseResult,\n    session: &GdbSession,\n    timeline: &HeapTimeline,\n    reader: &EventFileReader,\n    _limits: &ExecutionLimits,\n    notes: &mut Vec<String>,\n) {\n    // Post-mortem events (destructors, exit handlers) may have landed after\n    // the final stop.\n    for ev in reader.read_new() {\n        // takes &mut reader normally; events were drained by the caller loop\n        let _ = ev;\n    }\n    let _ = timeline;\n    let (_, total, truncated) = session.program_output();\n    result.program_output_bytes = total;\n    result.program_output_truncated = truncated;\n    if truncated {\n        result.limits_triggered.push(\"max_output_bytes\".into());\n    }\n    if timeline.blocks_capped {\n        result.limits_triggered.push(\"max_heap_allocations\".into());\n    }\n    if timeline.events_capped {\n        notes.push(\"allocation event history cap reached; later events dropped\".into());\n    }\n    if !reader.parse_errors.is_empty() {\n        notes.push(format!(\n            \"{} allocation event line(s) failed to parse\",\n            reader.parse_errors.len()\n        ));\n    }\n}\n\n/// Capture GDB state, degrading to an empty capture on failure (e.g. dead\n/// inferior) instead of losing the stop.\nasync fn capture_or_empty(session: &mut GdbSession, opts: &CaptureOptions) -> crate::gdb_mi::CapturedState {\n    match capture_state(session, opts).await {\n        Ok(state) => state,\n        Err(_) => crate::gdb_mi::CapturedState::default(),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Drain events and read the live heap for the current stop.\nasync fn read_events_and_heap(\n    session: &mut GdbSession,\n    timeline: &mut HeapTimeline,\n    reader: &mut EventFileReader,\n    result: &mut GdbPhaseResult,\n    limits: &ExecutionLimits,\n    pid: Option<u32>,\n) {\n    for ev in reader.read_new() {\n        timeline.ingest(&ev);\n    }\n    let Some(pid) = pid else { return };\n    let blocks = timeline.alive_blocks(pid);\n    if blocks.is_empty() {\n        return;\n    }\n    // Budget is applied by the caller via push_snapshot; here we only ingest.\n    let _ = (result, limits);\n}\n\n/// Build and append one snapshot (with live heap reads inside the budget).\n#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\nasync fn push_snapshot(\n    result: &mut GdbPhaseResult,\n    session: &mut GdbSession,\n    stop: &StoppedInfo,\n    state: &crate::gdb_mi::CapturedState,\n    timeline: &HeapTimeline,\n    pid: Option<u32>,\n    limits: &ExecutionLimits,\n    snapshot_cap_noted: &mut bool,\n    memory_cap_noted: &mut bool,\n    read_cap_noted: &mut bool,\n    notes: &mut Vec<String>,\n) {\n    if result.snapshots.len() >= limits.max_snapshot_count {\n        if !*snapshot_cap_noted {\n            result.limits_triggered.push(\"max_snapshot_count\".into());\n            *snapshot_cap_noted = true;\n        }\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // Live heap reads within the remaining per-snapshot budget.\n    let mut heap_blocks: Vec<HeapBlockInfo> = Vec::new();\n    let mut memory_truncated = state.memory_used >= limits.max_snapshot_memory_bytes;\n    if let Some(pid) = pid {\n        let budget = limits.max_snapshot_memory_bytes.saturating_sub(state.memory_used);\n        let alive = timeline.alive_blocks(pid);\n        let over_block_cap = alive.len() > MAX_HEAP_BLOCKS_PER_SNAPSHOT;\n        for block in alive.into_iter().take(MAX_HEAP_BLOCKS_PER_SNAPSHOT) {\n            let addr = format!(\"0x{:x}\", block.addr);\n            let read_size = (block.size.min(limits.max_memory_read_bytes as u64)) as usize;\n            let mut info = HeapBlockInfo {\n                allocation_id: block.allocation_id,\n                address: addr.clone(),\n                size_bytes: block.size,\n                allocation_type: block.alloc_type.to_string(),\n                is_freed: false,\n                allocation_file: block.caller_file.clone(),\n                allocation_line: block.caller_line,\n                raw_bytes_hex: None,\n                memory_read_error: None,\n                realloc_from_id: block.realloc_from_id,\n            };\n            if block.size as usize > limits.max_memory_read_bytes && !*read_cap_noted {\n                result.limits_triggered.push(\"max_memory_read_bytes\".into());\n                *read_cap_noted = true;\n            }\n            if read_size == 0 || memory_truncated {\n                info.memory_read_error = Some(\"snapshot memory budget exhausted\".into());\n                memory_truncated = true;\n                heap_blocks.push(info);\n                continue;\n            }\n            match session.read_memory_bytes(&addr, read_size as u64).await {\n                Ok(hex) => info.raw_bytes_hex = Some(hex),\n                Err(e) => info.memory_read_error = Some(e),\n            }\n            heap_blocks.push(info);\n        }\n        if over_block_cap {\n            memory_truncated = true;\n            notes.push(format!(\n                \"snapshot {} heap truncated to {} blocks\",\n                result.snapshots.len(),\n                MAX_HEAP_BLOCKS_PER_SNAPSHOT\n            ));\n        }\n    }\n    if memory_truncated && !*memory_cap_noted {\n        result.limits_triggered.push(\"max_snapshot_memory_bytes\".into());\n        *memory_cap_noted = true;\n    }\n\n    // Program output accumulated so far (head-truncated per snapshot).\n    let (output, _, output_truncated) = session.program_output();\n    let stdout_head = char_safe_head(&output, STDOUT_HEAD_CAP);\n\n    let frame = state\n        .current\n        .clone()\n        .or_else(|| stop.frame.clone())\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    result.snapshots.push(ExecutionSnapshot {\n        step_index: result.snapshots.len(),\n        file: frame.file.unwrap_or_default(),\n        line: frame.line.unwrap_or(0),\n        func: frame.func,\n        call_stack: state.frames.clone(),\n        variables: state.variables.clone(),\n        heap_blocks,\n        stdout_so_far: stdout_head,\n        stopped_reason: stop.reason.clone(),\n        signal: stop.signal_name.clone(),\n        memory_truncated,\n        stdout_truncated: output_truncated,\n    });\n}\n\nfn char_safe_head(s: &str, cap_bytes: usize) -> String {\n    if s.len() <= cap_bytes {\n        return s.to_string();\n    }\n    let mut cut = cap_bytes;\n    while !s.is_char_boundary(cut) {\n        cut -= 1;\n    }\n    s[..cut].to_string()\n}\n\nfn crash_from(stop: &StoppedInfo, state: &crate::gdb_mi::CapturedState) -> CrashReport {\n    let frame = stop.frame.clone().or_else(|| state.current.clone());\n    CrashReport {\n        signal_name: stop.signal_name.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| \"unknown\".into()),\n        file: frame.as_ref().and_then(|f| f.file.clone()),\n        line: frame.as_ref().and_then(|f| f.line),\n        func: frame.as_ref().map(|f| f.func.clone()).filter(|s| !s.is_empty()),\n        asan_summary: None,\n        backtrace: state.frames.clone(),\n        detail: stop.signal_meaning.clone(),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Inferior exit code: from the stop record, else from the\n/// `=thread-group-exited` notification in the backlog. MI emits the value as\n/// a decimal-or-hex string depending on version; both are accepted.\nfn exit_code_from(session: &GdbSession, stop: &StoppedInfo) -> Option<i32> {\n    if let Some(code) = &stop.exit_code {\n        return parse_mi_exit_code(code);\n    }\n    for record in session.take_backlog() {\n        if let crate::mi_parser::MiRecord::Notify { class, results } = &record {\n            if class == \"thread-group-exited\" {\n                for r in results {\n                    if r.variable == \"exit-code\" {\n                        if let Some(v) = crate::mi_parser::as_const(&r.value) {\n                            if let Some(c) = parse_mi_exit_code(v) {\n                                return Some(c);\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\nfn parse_mi_exit_code(text: &str) -> Option<i32> {\n    if let Ok(v) = text.parse::<i32>() {\n        return Some(v);\n    }\n    u32::from_str_radix(text, 16).ok().map(|v| v as i32)\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Timeline helpers\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nfn infer_parent_pid(timeline: &HeapTimeline, inferior_pid: Option<u32>) -> Option<u32> {\n    if let Some(pid) = inferior_pid {\n        return Some(pid);\n    }\n    let pids = timeline.pids_seen();\n    if pids.len() == 1 {\n        Some(pids[0])\n    } else {\n        None\n    }\n}\n\n/// Fill snapshot heap blocks with resolved allocation locations and global\n/// (pid-widened) ids.\nfn backfill_snapshots(\n    timeline: &HeapTimeline,\n    mut snapshots: Vec<ExecutionSnapshot>,\n    parent_pid:                    notes.push(\"valgrind XML could not be parsed (execution terminated?)\".into());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => notes.push(format!(\"valgrind failed: {e}\")),\n        }\n    }\n\n    // ---- assemble ------------------------------------------------------------\n    let parent_pid = infer_parent_pid(&timeline, phase.inferior_pid);\n    trace.snapshots = backfill_snapshots(&timeline, phase.snapshots, parent_pid);\n    trace.heap_events = final_events(&timeline);\n    trace.heap_state = build_heap_state(&timeline, &trace.snapshots, parent_pid);\n    trace.crash_report = crash;\n    trace.sanitizer_report = sanitizer_report;\n    trace.valgrind_report = valgrind_report;\n\n    if timeline.blocks_capped {\n        notes.push(format!(\n            \"allocation block cap reached ({}); later allocations recorded as events only\",\n            limits.max_heap_allocations\n        ));\n    }\n\n    trace.resource_usage = ResourceUsage {\n        wall_time_ms: started.elapsed().as_millis() as u64,\n        gdb_commands_issued: phase.commands_issued,\n        snapshots_captured: trace.snapshots.len(),\n        allocation_events_ingested: trace.heap_events.len(),\n        program_output_bytes: phase.program_output_bytes,\n        program_output_truncated: phase.program_output_truncated,\n        limits_triggered: phase.limits_triggered.clone(),\n        inferior_exit_code: phase.exit_code,\n    };\n    trace.execution_status = status;\n    trace.analysis_notes = notes;\n    meta.cgroup_enforced = phase.cgroup_enforced;\n    trace.session_meta = Some(meta);\n\n    if !config.keep_temp {\n        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&session_dir);\n    }\n    Ok(trace)\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// GDB phase\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n/// Everything the GDB execution phase produced.\npub struct GdbPhaseResult {\n    pub status: ExecutionStatus,\n    pub crash: Option<CrashReport>,\n    pub exit_code: Option<i32>,\n    pub inferior_pid: Option<u32>,\n    pub commands_issued: u64,\n    pub limits_triggered: Vec<String>,\n    pub program_output_bytes: u64,\n    pub program_output_truncated: bool,\n    pub snapshots: Vec<ExecutionSnapshot>,\n    pub cgroup_enforced: bool,\n}\n\n/// Run the debug binary under GDB/MI2, stepping through user code and\n/// capturing one snapshot per stop, with live heap contents read through the\n/// debugger at each snapshot. Allocation events are ingested after every\n/// stop. Never loses partial results: any stop condition (exit, crash,\n/// timeout, step limit) terminates the loop gracefully.\n#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\npub async fn run_gdb_phase(\n    config: &TraceConfig,\n    limits: &ExecutionLimits,\n    classifier: &UserCodeClassifier,\n    binary: &Path,\n    event_file: &Path,\n    reader: &mut EventFileReader,\n    timeline: &mut HeapTimeline,\n    notes: &mut Vec<String>,\n) -> Result<GdbPhaseResult> {\n    let timeout_secs = limits.timeout_seconds.max(1);\n    let wall_deadline = Instant::now()\n        + Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs * WALL_TIMEOUT_FACTOR + WALL_TIMEOUT_SLACK_SECS);\n\n    let mut result = GdbPhaseResult {\n        status: ExecutionStatus::ExecutionFailure,\n        crash: None,\n        exit_code: None,\n        inferior_pid: None,\n        commands_issued: 0,\n        limits_triggered: Vec::new(),\n        program_output_bytes: 0,\n        program_output_truncated: false,\n        snapshots: Vec::new(),\n        cgroup_enforced: false,\n    };\n\n    // Best-effort cgroup v2 enforcement for the inferior tree.\n    let cgroup = CgroupGuard::create(limits);\n\n    let inferior_dir = config\n        .inferior_working_directory\n        .clone()\n        .or_else(|| config.build.working_directory.clone());\n    let launch_opts = GdbLaunchOptions {\n        binary: binary.to_path_buf(),\n        working_directory: inferior_dir.clone(),\n        program_args: config.program_args.clone(),\n        limits: limits.clone(),\n        // The inferior inherits GDB's environment; the C runtime reads\n        // C_TRACE_EVENT_FILE to find its dedicated event trace file.\n        env: vec![(\n            \"C_TRACE_EVENT_FILE\".into(),\n            event_file.display().to_string(),\n        )],\n    };\n\n    let mut session = match GdbSession::launch(&launch_opts).await {\n        Ok(s) => s,\n        Err(e) => {\n            notes.push(format!(\"could not launch gdb: {e}\"));\n            result.status = ExecutionStatus::DebuggerFailure;\n            return Ok(result);\n        }\n    };\n    result.commands_issued = session.commands_issued.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);\n\n    // Breakpoint at main; without it we can still run to completion (no\n    // stepping, no snapshots before exit).\n    let have_breakpoint = match session.insert_breakpoint(\"main\").await {\n        Ok(_) => true,\n        Err(e) => {\n            notes.push(format!(\"no breakpoint at main ({e}); running to completion\"));\n            false\n        }\n    };\n\n    // Run the inferior; the first stop is the breakpoint (or exit).\n    let run_timeout = remaining(wall_deadline).min(Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs * 2 + 10));\n    let mut stop = match session.run(run_timeout).await {\n        Ok(stop) => stop,\n        Err(e) => {\n            notes.push(format!(\"gdb run failed: {e}\"));\n            if remaining(wall_deadline).is_zero() {\n                result.status = ExecutionStatus::Timeout;\n                result.limits_triggered.push(\"timeout_seconds\".into());\n            } else {\n                result.status = ExecutionStatus::ExecutionFailure;\n            }\n            terminate(&mut session, cgroup.as_ref()).await;\n            finish_phase(&mut result, &session, timeline, reader, notes);\n            return Ok(result);\n        }\n    };\n    result.inferior_pid = session.inferior_pid;\n    if let (Some(cg), Some(pid)) = (cgroup.as_ref(), session.inferior_pid) {\n        result.cgroup_enforced = cg.attach(pid);\n        if !result.cgroup_enforced {\n            notes.push(\n                \"cgroup v2 enforcement unavailable (not delegated); using rlimits only\".into(),\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    let capture_opts = CaptureOptions {\n        classifier: classifier.clone(),\n        max_variables: limits.max_variables_per_snapshot,\n        max_memory_read: limits.max_memory_read_bytes,\n        memory_budget: limits.max_snapshot_memory_bytes,\n    };\n\n    let mut steps: usize = 0;\n    let mut finish_chain: usize = 0;\n    let mut snapshot_cap_noted = false;\n    let mut memory_cap_noted = false;\n    let mut read_cap_noted = false;\n\n    loop {\n        // Ingest allocation events emitted since the last stop. The inferior\n        // is stopped here, so the event file is complete up to now.\n        for ev in reader.read_new() {\n            timeline.ingest(&ev);\n        }\n\n        // --- classify the stop ---------------------------------------------------\n        if stop.is_exit() {\n            result.exit_code = exit_code_from(&session, &stop);\n            result.status = ExecutionStatus::Completed;\n            break;\n        }\n        if stop.is_signal() {\n            match classify_signal(stop.signal_name.as_deref()) {\n                SignalClass::Fatal => {\n                    // Capture the crash state (registers are still valid).\n                    let state = capture_or_empty(&mut session, &capture_opts).await;\n                    push_snapshot(\n                        &mut result,\n                        &mut session,\n                        &stop,\n                        &state,\n                        timeline,\n                        inferior_pid_of(&session),\n                        limits,\n                        &mut snapshot_cap_noted,\n                        &mut memory_cap_noted,\n                        &mut read_cap_noted,\n                        notes,\n                    )\n                    .await;\n                    result.crash = Some(crash_from(&stop, &state));\n                    result.status = ExecutionStatus::Crashed;\n                    break;\n                }\n                SignalClass::Resource => {\n                    result.status = ExecutionStatus::ResourceLimitReached;\n                    result\n                        .limits_triggered\n                        .push(stop.signal_name.clone().unwrap_or_default());\n                    break;\n                }\n                SignalClass::Benign => {\n                    // Resume execution; counts as a step so signal storms are\n                    // bounded by max_steps.\n                    steps += 1;\n                    if steps > limits.max_steps {\n                        result.status = ExecutionStatus::StepLimitReached;\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    if Instant::now() >= wall_deadline {\n                        result.status = ExecutionStatus::Timeout;\n                        result.limits_triggered.push(\"timeout_seconds\".into());\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    stop = match session.exec_continue(step_timeout(wall_deadline)).await {\n                        Ok(s) => s,\n                        Err(e) => {\n                            notes.push(format!(\"continue after benign signal failed: {e}\"));\n                            result.status = ExecutionStatus::ExecutionFailure;\n                            break;\n                        }\n                    };\n                    continue;\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // --- capture snapshot (exit stops broke out above) ------------------------\n        let state = capture_or_empty(&mut session, &capture_opts).await;\n        push_snapshot(\n            &mut result,\n            &mut session,\n            &stop,\n            &state,\n            timeline,\n            inferior_pid_of(&session),\n            limits,\n            &mut snapshot_cap_noted,\n            &mut memory_cap_noted,\n            &mut read_cap_noted,\n            notes,\n        )\n        .await;\n\n        // --- resource checks -------------------------------------------------------\n        if Instant::now() >= wall_deadline {\n            result.status = ExecutionStatus::Timeout;\n            result.limits_triggered.push(\"timeout_seconds\".into());\n            break;\n        }\n        if steps >= limits.max_steps {\n            result.status = ExecutionStatus::StepLimitReached;\n            break;\n        }\n\n        // --- decide the next stepping command ---------------------------------------\n        let is_user = state.is_user_code;\n        let next_stop = if is_user || !have_breakpoint {\n            // User code: single-step (this enters calls too, which is how we\n            // visit helper functions in the user's project).\n            steps += 1;\n            finish_chain = 0;\n            match session.exec_step(step_timeout(wall_deadline)).await {\n                Ok(s) => s,\n                Err(EngineError::GdbCommandTimeout { .. }) => {\n                    // The inferior hung inside a step (blocking syscall, long\n                    // loop): preserve partials and report the timeout.\n                    result.status = ExecutionStatus::Timeout;\n                    result.limits_triggered.push(\"timeout_seconds\".into());\n                    break;\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    notes.push(format!(\"step failed: {e}\"));\n                    result.status = ExecutionStatus::ExecutionFailure;\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n        } else {\n            // Non-user frame: run until this frame returns so we come back\n            // into user code without single-stepping the standard library.\n            if finish_chain >= MAX_FINISH_CHAIN {\n                steps += 1;\n                match session.exec_continue(step_timeout(wall_deadline)).await {\n                    Ok(s) => s,\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        notes.push(format!(\"continue failed: {e}\"));\n                        result.status = ExecutionStatus::ExecutionFailure;\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n            } else {\n                finish_chain += 1;\n                match session.exec_finish(step_timeout(wall_deadline)).await {\n                    Ok(s) => s,\n                    Err(EngineError::GdbCommandError { message, .. })\n                        if message.contains(\"finish not meaningful\") =>\n                    {\n                        // Outermost frame: the program is finishing; continue.\n                        steps += 1;\n                        match session.exec_continue(step_timeout(wall_deadline)).await {\n                            Ok(s) => s,\n                            Err(e) => {\n                                notes.push(format!(\"continue failed: {e}\"));\n                                result.status = ExecutionStatus::ExecutionFailure;\n                                break;\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                    Err(EngineError::GdbCommandTimeout { .. }) => {\n                        result.status = ExecutionStatus::Timeout;\n                        result.limits_triggered.push(\"timeout_seconds\".into());\n                        break;\n                    }\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        notes.push(format!(\"finish failed: {e}\"));\n                        result.status = ExecutionStatus::ExecutionFailure;\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        };\n        // The finish chain resets once execution is back in user code.\n        if let Some(frame) = &next_stop.frame {\n            if classifier.is_user_file(frame) {\n                finish_chain = 0;\n            }\n        }\n        stop = next_stop;\n    }\n\n    // --- termination -----------------------------------------------------------\n    match result.status {\n        // Normal and crash endings: GDB shuts down gracefully.\n        ExecutionStatus::Completed | ExecutionStatus::Crashed => {\n            terminate(&mut session, cgroup.as_ref()).await;\n        }\n        // Limit endings: hard-kill the inferior tree so nothing survives.\n        ExecutionStatus::Timeout\n        | ExecutionStatus::StepLimitReached\n        | ExecutionStatus::ResourceLimitReached\n        | ExecutionStatus::ExecutionFailure\n        | ExecutionStatus::DebuggerFailure => {\n            if let Some(cg) = cgroup.as_ref() {\n                cg.kill_all();\n            }\n            session.kill().await;\n        }\n        ExecutionStatus::CompileFailed => {\n            terminate(&mut session, cgroup.as_ref()).await;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Post-mortem events (destructors, exit handlers) may have landed after\n    // the final stop.\n    for ev in reader.read_new() {\n        timeline.ingest(&ev);\n    }\n    finish_phase(&mut result, &session, timeline, reader, notes);\n    Ok(result)\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Phase helpers\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nenum SignalClass {\n    Fatal,\n    Resource,\n    Benign,\n}\n\nfn classify_signal(name: Option<&str>) -> SignalClass {\n    match name {\n        Some(n) if FATAL_SIGNALS.contains(&n) => SignalClass::Fatal,\n        Some(n) if RESOURCE_SIGNALS.contains(&n) => SignalClass::Resource,\n        Some(n) if BENIGN_SIGNALS.contains(&n) => SignalClass::Benign,\n        // Unknown signal: conservatively fatal so we stop and report it.\n        _ => SignalClass::Fatal,\n    }\n}\n\nfn remaining(deadline: Instant) -> Duration {\n    deadline.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now())\n}\n\nfn step_timeout(wall_deadline: Instant) -> Duration {\n    remaining(wall_deadline)\n        .min(PER_STEP_TIMEOUT)\n        .max(Duration::from_secs(1))\n}\n\nfn inferior_pid_of(session: &GdbSession) -> Option<u32> {\n    session.inferior_pid\n}\n\n/// Graceful shutdown (normal end): cgroup kill is a no-op safety net and GDB\n/// exits cleanly, closing the pty.\nasync fn terminate(session: &mut GdbSession, cgroup: Option<&CgroupGuard>) {\n    if let Some(cg) = cgroup {\n        cg.kill_all();\n    }\n    session.kill().await;\n}\n\n/// Finalize a phase result: output counters, cap notes.\nfn finish_phase(\n    result: &mut GdbPhaseResult,\n    session: &GdbSession,\n    timeline: &HeapTimeline,\n    reader: &EventFileReader,\n    notes: &mut Vec<String>,\n) {\n    result.commands_issued = session.commands_issued.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::SeqCst);\n    let (_, total, truncated) = session.program_output();\n    result.program_output_bytes = total;\n    result.program_output_truncated = truncated;\n    if truncated {\n        result.limits_triggered.push(\"max_output_bytes\".into());\n    }\n    if timeline.blocks_capped && !result.limits_triggered.contains(&\"max_heap_allocations\".into()) {\n        result.limits_triggered.push(\"max_heap_allocations\".into());\n    }\n    if timeline.events_capped {\n        notes.push(\"allocation event history cap reached; later events dropped\".into());\n    }\n    if !reader.parse_errors.is_empty() {\n        notes.push(format!(\n            \"{} allocation event line(s) failed to parse\",\n            reader.parse_errors.len()\n        ));\n    }\n}\n\n/// Capture GDB state, degrading to an empty capture on failure (e.g. dead\n/// inferior) instead of losing the stop.\nasync fn capture_or_empty(\n    session: &mut GdbSession,\n    opts: &CaptureOptions,\n) -> crate::gdb_mi::CapturedState {\n    match capture_state(session, opts).await {\n        Ok(state) => state,\n        Err(_) => crate::gdb_mi::CapturedState::default(),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Build and append one snapshot (with live heap reads inside the budget).\n#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]\nasync fn push_snapshot(\n    result: &mut GdbPhaseResult,\n    session: &mut GdbSession,\n    stop: &StoppedInfo,\n    state: &crate::gdb_mi::CapturedState,\n    timeline: &HeapTimeline,\n    pid: Option<u32>,\n    limits: &ExecutionLimits,\n    snapshot_cap_noted: &mut bool,\n    memory_cap_noted: &mut bool,\n    read_cap_noted: &mut bool,\n    notes: &mut Vec<String>,\n) {\n    if result.snapshots.len() >= limits.max_snapshot_count {\n        if !*snapshot_cap_noted {\n            result.limits_triggered.push(\"max_snapshot_count\".into());\n            *snapshot_cap_noted = true;\n        }\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // Live heap reads within the remaining per-snapshot budget (the budget is\n    // shared with the variable raw-byte reads performed by capture_state).\n    let mut heap_blocks: Vec<HeapBlockInfo> = Vec::new();\n    let mut budget_left = limits\n        .max_snapshot_memory_bytes\n        .saturating_sub(state.memory_used);\n    let mut memory_truncated = budget_left == 0;\n    if let Some(pid) = pid {\n        let alive = timeline.alive_blocks(pid);\n        let over_block_cap = alive.len() > MAX_HEAP_BLOCKS_PER_SNAPSHOT;\n        for block in alive.into_iter().take(MAX_HEAP_BLOCKS_PER_SNAPSHOT) {\n            let addr = format!(\"0x{:x}\", block.addr);\n            let read_size = block\n                .size\n                .min(limits.max_memory_read_bytes as u64)\n                .min(budget_left as u64) as usize;\n            let mut info = HeapBlockInfo {\n                allocation_id: block.allocation_id,\n                address: addr.clone(),\n                size_bytes: block.size,\n                allocation_type: block.alloc_type.to_string(),\n                is_freed: false,\n                allocation_file: block.caller_file.clone(),\n                allocation_line: block.caller_line,\n                raw_bytes_hex: None,\n                memory_read_error: None,\n                realloc_from_id: block.realloc_from_id,\n            };\n            if block.size as usize > limits.max_memory_read_bytes && !*read_cap_noted {\n                result.limits_triggered.push(\"max_memory_read_bytes\".into());\n                *read_cap_noted = true;\n            }\n            if read_size == 0 {\n                info.memory_read_error = Some(\"snapshot memory budget exhausted\".into());\n                memory_truncated = true;\n                heap_blocks.push(info);\n                continue;\n            }\n            match session.read_memory_bytes(&addr, read_size as u64).await {\n                Ok(hex) => info.raw_bytes_hex = Some(hex),\n                Err(e) => info.memory_read_error = Some(format!(\"memory read failed: {e}\")),\n            }\n            budget_left = budget_left.saturating_sub(read_size);\n            if read_size < block.size as usize {\n                memory_truncated = true; // partial capture\n            }\n            heap_blocks.push(info);\n        }\n        if over_block_cap {\n            memory_truncated = true;\n            notes.push(format!(\n                \"snapshot {} heap truncated to {} blocks\",\n                result.snapshots.len(),\n                MAX_HEAP_BLOCKS_PER_SNAPSHOT\n            ));\n        }\n    }\n    if memory_truncated && !*memory_cap_noted {\n        result.limits_triggered.push(\"max_snapshot_memory_bytes\".into());\n        *memory_cap_noted = true;\n    }\n\n    // Program output accumulated so far (head-truncated per snapshot).\n    let (output, _, output_truncated) = session.program_output();\n    let stdout_head = char_safe_head(&output, STDOUT_HEAD_CAP);\n\n    let frame = state\n        .current\n        .clone()\n        .or_else(|| stop.frame.clone())\n        .unwrap_or_default();\n    result.snapshots.push(ExecutionSnapshot {\n        step_index: result.snapshots.len(),\n        file: frame.file.unwrap_or_default(),\n        line: frame.line.unwrap_or(0),\n        func: frame.func,\n        call_stack: state.frames.clone(),\n        variables: state.variables.clone(),\n        heap_blocks,\n        stdout_so_far: stdout_head,\n        stopped_reason: stop.reason.clone(),\n        signal: stop.signal_name.clone(),\n        memory_truncated,\n        stdout_truncated: output_truncated,\n    });\n}\n\nfn char_safe_head(s: &str, cap_bytes: usize) -> String {\n    if s.len() <= cap_bytes {\n        return s.to_string();\n    }\n    let mut cut = cap_bytes;\n    while !s.is_char_boundary(cut) {\n        cut -= 1;\n    }\n    s[..cut].to_string()\n}\n\nfn crash_from(stop: &StoppedInfo, state: &crate::gdb_mi::CapturedState) -> CrashReport {\n    let frame = stop.frame.clone().or_else(|| state.current.clone());\n    CrashReport {\n        signal_name: stop\n            .signal_name\n            .clone()\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| \"unknown\".into()),\n        file: frame.as_ref().and_then(|f| f.file.clone()),\n        line: frame.as_ref().and_then(|f| f.line),\n        func: frame\n            .as_ref()\n            .map(|f| f.func.clone())\n            .filter(|s| !s.is_empty()),\n        asan_summary: None,\n        backtrace: state.frames.clone(),\n        detail: stop.signal_meaning.clone(),\n    }\n}\n\n/// Inferior exit code: from the stop record, else from the\n/// `=thread-group-exited` notification in the backlog. MI emits the value as\n/// decimal in current versions but hex in some older ones; both accepted.\nfn exit_code_from(session: &mut GdbSession, stop: &StoppedInfo) -> Option<i32> {\n    if let Some(code) = &stop.exit_code {\n        return parse_mi_exit_code(code);\n    }\n    for record in session.take_backlog() {\n        if let crate::mi_parser::MiRecord::Notify { class, results } = &record {\n            if class == \"thread-group-exited\" {\n                for r in results {\n                    if r.variable == \"exit-code\" {\n                        if let Some(v) = crate::mi_parser::as_const(&r.value) {\n                            if let Some(c) = parse_mi_exit_code(v) {\n                                return Some(c);\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\nfn parse_mi_exit_code(text: &str) -> Option<i32> {\n    if let Ok(v) = text.parse::<i32>() {\n        return Some(v);\n    }\n    u32::from_str_radix(text, 16).ok().map(|v| v as i32)\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Timeline helpers\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nfn infer_parent_pid(timeline: &HeapTimeline, inferior_pid: Option<u32>) -> Option<u32> {\n    if let Some(pid) = inferior_pid {\n        return Some(pid);\n    }\n    let pids = timeline.pids_seen();\n    if pids.len() == 1 {\n        Some(pids[0])\n    } else {\n        None\n    }\n}\n\n/// Fill snapshot heap blocks with resolved allocation locations and global\n/// (pid-widened) ids.\nfn backfill_snapshots(\n    timeline: &HeapTimeline,\n    mut snapshots: Vec<ExecutionSnapshot>,\n    parent_pid: Option<u32>,\n) -> Vec<ExecutionSnapshot> {\n    let Some(parent_pid) = parent_pid else {\n        return snapshots;\n    };\n    for snap in snapshots.iter_mut() {\n        for block in snap.heap_blocks.iter_mut() {\n            if let Some(state) = timeline.block_by_id(parent_pid, block.allocation_id) {\n                block.allocation_file = state.caller_file.clone();\n                block.allocation_line = state.caller_line;\n                block.realloc_from_id = state\n                    .realloc_from_id\n                    .map(|id| timeline.global_id(parent_pid, id));\n                block.allocation_id = timeline.global_id(parent_pid, block.allocation_id);\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    snapshots\n}\n\n/// Serialized heap events with pid-widened ids when multiple processes ran.\nfn final_events(timeline: &HeapTimeline) -> Vec<crate::models::HeapEvent> {\n    timeline\n        .events()\n        .iter()\n        .map(|e| {\n            let mut e = e.clone();\n            e.allocation_id = timeline.global_id(e.pid, e.allocation_id);\n            if let Some(old) = e.old_allocation_id {\n                e.old_allocation_id = Some(timeline.global_id(e.pid, old));\n            }\n            e\n        })\n        .collect()\n}\n\n/// Final heap state: every reconstructed block with its end-of-run status.\n/// `raw_bytes_hex` carries the last bytes captured while the block was alive\n/// (from any snapshot); freed blocks keep that historical capture, live\n/// blocks the most recent one.\nfn build_heap_state(\n    timeline: &HeapTimeline,\n    snapshots: &[ExecutionSnapshot],\n    parent_pid: Option<u32>,\n) -> Vec<HeapBlockInfo> {\n    let mut last_contents: HashMap<u64, String> = HashMap::new();\n    for snap in snapshots {\n        for b in &snap.heap_blocks {\n            if let Some(hex) = &b.raw_bytes_hex {\n                last_contents.insert(b.allocation_id, hex.clone());\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    timeline\n        .blocks()\n        .iter()\n        .map(|b| {\n            let global = parent_pid\n                .map(|p| timeline.global_id(b.pid, b.allocation_id))\n                .unwrap_or(b.allocation_id);\n            HeapBlockInfo {\n                allocation_id: global,\n                address: format!(\"0x{:x}\", b.addr),\n                size_bytes: b.size,\n                allocation_type: b.alloc_type.to_string(),\n                is_freed: b.freed,\n                allocation_file: pub object_file: Vec<PathBuf>,\n\n    /// Executable name (defaults to a session-unique name).\n    #[arg(long)]\n    pub output_name: Option<String>,\n\n    /// Working directory for compilation (and 285:     /// Send one MI command and await its token-matched result.
286:     pub async fn execute(&mut self, command: &str) -> Result<MiCommandResponse> {
287:         let command = command.trim();
288:         if self.shared.eof.load(Ordering::SeqCst) {
289:             return Err(EngineError::Gdb("gdb session already closed".into()));
290:         }
291:         let token = self.next_token;
292:         self.next_token += 1;
293:         self.commands_issued.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
294: 
295:         // Streams accumulated by earlier commands (or by async chatter) must
296:         // not leak into this command's response.
297:         self.shared.current_streams.lock().unwrap().clear();
298: 
299:         let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
300:         self.shared.pending.lock().unwrap().insert(token, tx);
301: 
302:         let line = format!("{}{}\n", token, command);
303:         if let Err(e) = self.stdin.write_all(line.as_bytes()).await {
304:             self.shared.eof.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
305:             return Err(EngineError::Gdb(format!("writing to gdb failed: {e}")));
306:         }
307:         if let Err(e) = self.stdin.flush().await {
308:             return Err(EngineError::Gdb(format!("flushing to gdb failed: {e}")));
309:         }
310: 
311:         match tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECS), rx).await {
312:             Ok(Ok(Ok((record, streams)))) => Ok(MiCommandResponse { record, streams }),
313:             Ok(Ok(Err(e))) => Err(EngineError::Gdb(e)),
314:             Ok(Err(_)) => {
315:                 self.shared.pending.lock().unwrap().remove(&token);
316:                 Err(EngineError::Gdb("gdb dropped the response channel".into()))
317:             }
318:             Err(_) => {
319:                 self.shared.pending.lock().unwrap().remove(&token);
320:                 Err(EngineError::GdbCommandTimeout {
321:                     command: command.to_string(),
322:                     timeout_secs: COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECS,
323:                 })
324:             }
325:         }
326:     }

328:     /// Await the next `*stopped` record, buffering unrelated async records.
329:     pub async fn wait_stopped(&mut self, timeout: Duration) -> Result<StoppedInfo> {
330:         let deadline = Instant::now() + timeout;
331:         loop {
332:             let remaining = deadline.saturating_duration_since(Instant::now());
333:             if remaining.is_zero() {
334:                 return Err(EngineError::Gdb("timed out waiting for *stopped".into()));
335:             }
336:             match tokio::time::timeout(remaining, self.async_rx.recv()).await {
337:                 Ok(Some(record)) => match &record {
338:                     MiRecord::Exec { class, .. } if class == "stopped" => {
339:                         return Ok(stopped_info_from(&record));
340:                     }
341:                     MiRecord::Notify { class, results } => {
342:                         self.note_notify(class, results);
343:                     }
344:                     _ => self.backlog.push(record),
345:                 },
346:                 Ok(None) => {
347:                     return Err(EngineError::Gdb("gdb exited before *stopped".into()))
348:                 }
349:                 Err(_) => {
350:                     return Err(EngineError::Gdb(format!(
351:                         "timed out after {:.1}s waiting for *stopped",
352:                         timeout.as_secs_f32()
353:                     )))
354:                 }
355:             }
356:         }
357:     }

async fn step_and_wait(&mut self, command: &str, timeout: Duration) -> Result<StoppedInfo> {
    let resp = self.execute(command).await?;

}

{
  "content": "# c-trace-engine\n\nA standalone Rust CLI that takes a configurable C project, compiles it with\nGCC, executes it under GDB/MI2 while recording execution snapshots and heap\nallocation events, runs an independent Valgrind analysis plus a separate\nsanitizer pass, and emits a single structured JSON\n[`DebugSessionTrace`](examples/example_trace.json).\n\nIt is the backend for a future offline-first visual C IDE: every artifact in\nthe trace — snapshots, variables, pointer links, heap blocks, allocation\nhistory, compiler diagnostics, crashes and memory-analysis findings — is\nderived from real observations of the program. The engine never fabricates\nvalues it could not observe; unobservable data is `null`.\n\n## Quick start\n\n```sh\ncargo run -- sample.c\n```\n\nwrites the trace to stdout and exits `0` on success. Useful variants:\n\n```sh\ncargo run -- sample.c --output trace.json          # also save to a file\ncargo run -- sample.c -- --verbose 42              # args for the program\ncargo run -- fixtures/c/multi_file/main.c --add-source fixtures/c/multi_file/helper.c\ncargo run -- sample.c --timeout 3 --max-steps 200 --max-snapshots 100\ncargo run -- sample.c --config build.json          # JSON BuildConfig file\ncargo run -- broken.c                              # exit code 2 + diagnostics\n```\n\n## Exit codes\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|------|---------|\n| `0`  | A trace was produced (execution completed, crashed, timed out, hit a limit). |\n| `2`  | Compilation failed; a partial trace with the compiler diagnostics is still emitted. |\n| `1`  | Operational error (bad arguments, missing source file, missing required tool). No trace. |\n\n## Trace contents (abridged)\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"execution_status\": \"completed | compile_failed | crashed | timeout | step_limit_reached | ...\",\n  \"compiled_successfully\": true,\n  \"compile_errors\": [ { \"file\": \"...\", \"line\": 1, \"column\": 15, \"kind\": \"error\", \"message\": \"...\" } ],\n  \"snapshots\": [                     // one per GDB stop in user code (bounded)\n    {\n      \"step_index\": 0, \"file\": \"sample.c\", \"line\": 30, \"func\": \"main\",\n      \"call_stack\": [...], \"variables\": [ { \"name\": \"arr\", \"c_type\": \"int *\",\n      \"value\": \"0x0\", \"address\": \"0x7fff...\", \"points_to\": \"0x0\", \"raw_bytes_hex\": \"...\" } ],\n      \"heap_blocks\": [ { \"allocation_id\": 1, \"address\": \"0x705010\", \"size_bytes\": 12,\n                         \"raw_bytes_hex\": \"00000000...\", \"allocation_file\": \"sample.c\",\n                         \"allocation_line\": 30 } ],\n      \"stdout_so_far\": \"...\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heap_events\":  [ { \"event_type\": \"allocated\", \"allocation_id\": 1, \"size_bytes\": 12 }, ... ],\n  \"heap_state\":   [ { \"allocation_id\": 1, \"allocation_type\": \"malloc\", \"is_freed\": false, ... } ],\n  \"crash_report\": { \"signal_name\": \"SIGSEGV\", \"file\": \"...\", \"line\": 7, \"backtrace\": [...],\n                    \"asan_summary\": \"SUMMARY: 455,\n                      \"snapshots_captured\": 26, \"limits_triggered\": [] },\n  \"session_meta\": { \"gcc_version\": \"...\", \"gdb_version\": \"...\", \"valgrind_version\": \"...\" }\n}\n```\n\nSee [`examples/example_trace.json`](examples/example_trace.json) for a full\nreal document produced by `cargo run -- sample.c`.\n\n## How it works\n\n```\n                     ┌──────────────┐\n  .c sources ───────▶│   compiler   │──▶ program_debug  (+ alloc_tracker.c)\n  BuildConfig ──────▶│  (GCC/SARIF) │──▶ program_asan   (sanitizers)\n                     └──────────────┘\n                            │\n                     ┌──────▼───────┐     pty (program stdout, never mixed with MI)\n                     │ gdb_mi.rs    │◀──▶ gdb --interpreter=mi2\n                     │ trace.rs     │     step / finish / continue loop\n                     └──────┬───────┘\n                            │  per stop: variables, frames, live heap reads\n                            ▼\n                     alloc_events.txt ◀── __wrap_malloc/calloc/realloc/free\n                     (dedicated file)      (link-time -Wl,--wrap instrumentation)\n                            │\n        ┌───────────────────┼────────────────────┐\n        ▼                   ▼                    ▼\n  Valgrind (XML)     sanitized run        addr2line batch\n  memcheck report    (crash pass only)    (caller file:line resolution)\n        └───────────────────┴────────────────────┘\n                            ▼\n                     DebugSessionTrace (JSON)\n```\n\n1. **Build** (`compiler.rs`): every translation unit is compiled with `-g -O0`\n   plus GCC's machine-readable diagnostics (`sarif-stderr` first, with\n   fallbacks for older GCC), linked with a small C runtime that intercepts\n   `malloc/calloc/realloc/free` via `-Wl,--wrap=...` and appends one event\n   line per operation to a dedicated trace file. A second, sanitizer-built\n   binary (ASan, plus UBSan when installed) is produced for the crash\n   diagnostic pass; if a sanitizer runtime is missing the engine degrades\n   and records a note.\n2. **Execute** (`gdb_mi.rs`, `trace.rs`): the debug binary runs under GDB in\n   MI2 mode with a token-matched command/response layer and a dedicated pty\n   for program output. The engine breaks at `main`, single-steps in user\n   code, and `finish`es out of non-user frames. {
  "content": "# Engine internals\n\nHow `c-trace-engine` observes a program. The guiding rules are:\n\n* **Never fabricate.** Everything in the trace came from a real observation\n  (compiler output, a GDB response, an event line, a tool report).\n* **Unobservable = `null`.** Fields the engine could not learn are absent or\n  `null`, not guessed.\n* **Partial results always survive.** Any stop condition degrades\n  gracefully and the trace records what happened in `analysis_notes`.\n\n## 1. Build & allocation instrumentation (`compiler.rs`, `c_runtime/alloc_tracker.c`)\n\nEach translation unit is compiled with `-g -O0 -fno-omit-frame-pointer` plus\nGCC 16's SARIF diagnostics on stderr (`-fdiagnostics-format=sarif-stderr`);\nolder GCC falls back to `-fdiagnostics-format=json` and then to plain text.\nGCC 16 emits **one SARIF document per translation unit** concatenated on\nstderr, so the parser consumes a *stream* of JSON documents\n(`serde_json::Deserializer::from_str(..).into_iter::<SarifDoc>()`).\n\nThe debug link embeds the C runtime (`alloc_tracker.c`) and redirects the\nprogram's allocator calls with `-Wl,--wrap=malloc --wrap=calloc\n--wrap=realloc --wrap=free`. The wrappers:\n\n* keep a small fixed-size process-local table of live blocks,\n* write **one line per operation** to the file named by\n  `C_TRACE_EVENT_FILE` (a dedicated file, never stdout/stderr, so program\n  output and telemetry cannot interleave or deadlock),\n* use a spinlock, no recursion and no allocation of their own — the tracker\n  must not perturb the allocator it observes,\n* assign per-process allocation ids; when an address is reused by a new\n  block it gets a fresh id, so `address` alone is never an identity,\n* report a **failed realloc** without freeing the original (glibc\n  semantics), and `realloc(p, 0)` as a free.\n\nEvent line format:\n\n```\n<pid> <seq> <kind> <id> <addr-hex> <size> <old_id> <old_addr-hex> <caller-hex> <status>\n```\n\n`kind` ∈ `malloc|calloc|realloc|free`; `status` ∈ `ok|ok_same|ok_moved|new|\nzero|failed|unknown|null`. `caller` is the return address of the allocator\ncall, resolved to `file:line` later by one batched `addr2line` run.\n\n`__wrap_malloc` forwards to `__real_malloc` etc.; this covers the\n*program's own* calls (and direct libc calls that land in the wrapped\nsymbols). Memory allocated inside libraries already linked against the real\nallocator is invisible to the timeline — Valgrind is the independent check\nthat sees everything.\n\n## 2. GDB session (`gdb_mi.rs`)\n\nThe session runs `gdb --nx --quiet --interpreter=mi2 <binary>` and speaks\nMI2 with:\n\n* **Token-matched commands**: every command is prefixed with a monotonically\n  increasing token; the matching result record resolves a oneshot channel.\n  Stream records (`~`, `&`, `@`) captured between command and response are\n  delivered with the response (needed for console-mode results such as\n  `whatis`).\n* **A dedicated pty for the inferior** via `-inferior-tty-set`: program\n  output never enters the MI stream. The master end is read by a tokio task\n  into a capped ring buffer (`max_output_bytes`).\n* **One channel** between reader task and session for async records\n  (`*running`, `*stopped`, `=notify`); the reader fails all pending\n  commands on EOF so a dead GDB never strands a wait.\n\nObserved GDB 18 behaviors the engine adapts to:\n\n* execution commands answer `^running` + async `*stopped` (including for\n  exits: `*stopped,reason=\"exited-normally\"`),\n* a `finish` from the outermost frame returns\n  `^error,msg=\"…finish… not meaningful in the outermost frame.\"`,\n* GDB occasionally reports a `*stopped` **without reason** after failing to\n  insert a temporary breakpoint while unwinding the outermost libc frame\n  (`Cannot insert breakpoint 0. Cannot access memory at address 0x101`).\n  Such stops cannot be finished; the engine continues instead, which lets\n  the imminent exit happen naturally,\n* GDB puts the inferior in its own process group, so killing GDB's group\n  does not kill the inferior — the engine kills both groups.\n\nTermination: every wait is timeout-bounded (per-command 20s, per-step 10s,\nsession wall = `4 × timeout_seconds + 30s`). On limit endings the engine\nkills the process groups (GDB's and the inferior's) and the cgroup subtree\nwhen available.\n\n## 3. Execution loop & snapshots (`trace.rs`)\n\n`run_gdb_phase` breaks at `main`, then:\n\n1. ingest allocation events that accumulated while the inferior ran,\n2. classify the stop: exit → `Completed` (+ exit code from the stop record\n   or `=thread-group-exited`); signal → fatal (`SIGSEGV`, `SIGABRT`, … →\n   `Crashed` + crash report), resource (`SIGXCPU`, `SIGKILL` →\n   `ResourceLimitReached`), benign (`SIGPIPE`, … → continue, bounded by the\n   step budget), no-reason stop → continue (see above),\n3. capture one snapshot:\n   * `-stack-list-frames` for the call stack,\n   * `-stack-list-variables --all-values` + `whatis` per variable for types,\n     own address, value and pointed-to address (`points_to`) — with raw\n     bytes read from the inferior within the per-snapshot budget,\n   * live heap blocks: for each tracked alive block one\n     `-data-read-memory-bytes` bounded by `max_memory_read_bytes` and the\n     remaining snapshot budget (blocks beyond the budget are recorded with\n     `memory_read_error`, not dropped),\n   * program output head (64 KiB cap per snapshot),\n4. step: `-exec-step` in user code; in non-user frames `-exec-finish`\n   (capped chain of 32, then `-exec-continue`).\n\nSnapshots are capped by `max_snapshot_count`; the memory budget is shared\nbetween variables and heap reads so one snapshot can never blow up the\ntrace.\n\n## 4. Heap reconstruction (`allocation_tracker.rs`)\n\n`HeapTimeline` ingests the raw event stream and reconstructs, per process:\n\n* **blocks** — one `BlockState` per allocation with allocation id, address,\n  size, type (`malloc`/`calloc`/`realloc`), realloc chain link\n  (`realloc_from_id`), caller pc, and final status (freed or still alive),\n* **events** — the full ordered history (allocated / reallocated / freed /\n  allocation_failed) with optional human-readable details (double free,\n  `free(NULL)`, failed realloc preserving the original),\n* **live byte counters** per process.\n\nIds are per-process; when a run produced more than one pid the serialized\nids are widened to `(pid << 32) | id` to stay unique across the trace —\nwith a single pid they stay plain (matches the C runtime's view).\n\nThe final `heap_state` lists every reconstructed block. A block's\n`raw_bytes_hex` is the last capture taken **while it was alive**; freed\nblocks keep that historical capture.\n\n## 5. Independent analyses\n\n**Valgrind** (`valgrind.rs`) runs the debug binary (without instrumentation\nwrappers — Valgrind replaces the allocator itself) under memcheck with\n`--xml=file --xml-user-prog-args`-style options, parses the XML with\n`roxmltree` (heap summary, error records with stacks, leak records) and\ncorrelates findings with allocation ids by `(file, line)` pairs resolved by\naddr2line. A Valgrind timeout leaves the partial XML; the engine notes it.\n\n**Sanitizer pass** (`sanitizer.rs`) runs only after a crash: the ASan-built\nbinary executes once with the same arguments and working directory; its\nstderr (`ERROR: AddressSanitizer: …`) is parsed into a structured report and\nthe `SUMMARY:` line is attached to the crash report as `asan_summary`.\nSanitizer runtimes are detected at link time: if libubsan is missing the\nbuild degrades to ASan-only, and if libasan is missing entirely the pass is\ndisabled with a note. Sanitizer and Valgrind children get CPU/file-size\nrlimits but **no address-space cap** — ASan maps terabytes of shadow memory\nand aborts under a small `RLIMIT_AS`.\n\n## 6. Resource controls (`resource_limits.rs`)\n\nLayered enforcement:\n\n1. **Engine clocks** — wall deadline, per-command and per-step timeouts;\n   every path is bounded, verified with real GDB.\n2. **rlimits** — `RLIMIT_CPU` (from `timeout_seconds`), `RLIMIT_FSIZE`,\n   `RLIMIT_NOFILE` on sanitizer/valgrind children. `RLIMIT_NPROC` is\n   deliberately never used: on Linux it is enforced per *real user id*, so\n   a low value breaks every `fork` on the whole desktop session\n   (empirically: `vfork: Resource temporarily unavailable` with 173 user\n   processes).\n3. **cgroup v2** — when a delegated subtree is writable, the inferior pid\n   is moved into it with `pids.max`, `memory.max` and `cpu.max`; on teardown\n   the subtree is killed (`cgroup.kill`). Best effort; its availability is\n   reported in `session_meta.cgroup_enforced`.\n\nThese limits protect the engine and the session — they are **not a\nsecurity sandbox** for hostile binaries.\n",
  "path": "/home/xe/Documents/visual_c/docs/engine-internals.md"
}

/// spawning of the inferior. Child-process budgets are therefore enforced
/// only through cgroup v2 `pids.max` when a delegated subtree is available

/// Configurable resource limits for a tracing session.
///
/// Defaults follow the engine's initial policy table (see README):
        assert_eq!(quote_for_mi("back\\slash"), "\"back\\\\slash\"");
    }

    #[test]
    fn user_code_classification() {
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("cte-cls-{}", std::process::id()));
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let src = dir.join("sample.c");
        std::fs::write(&src, "int main(void){return 0;}\n").unwrap();
        let mut build = crate::config::BuildConfig::default();
        build.source_file = src.clone();
        let cls = UserCodeClassifier::from_build(&build);
        let user_frame = StackFrameInfo {
            level: 0,
            func: "main".into(),
            file: Some("sample.c".into()),
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }

    #[test]
    fn program_buffer_cap() {
        let mut buf = ProgramBuffer::default();
        buf.push(&vec![b'a'; 100], 50);
        assert_eq!(buf.data.len(), 50);
        assert!(buf.truncated);

All nine stages are complete. The engine works end-to-end.

## What was blocking (and how it was fixed)

The session began with the end-to-end run hanging. Diagnosed with `ps`/`/proc` inspection and a raw MI-stream echo, three real bugs were found and fixed:

1. **addr2line pipe deadlock** (the actual hang): `ChildStdin::shutdown()` in tokio only flushes — it does **not** close the descriptor, so addr2line blocked in `anon_pipe_read` forever while the engine waited on stdout that would never EOF. Fixed by dropping the stdin handle after writing (true EOF) and wrapping both stages in 30s timeouts (`allocation_tracker.rs`).
2. **GDB "no-reason" stops**: finishing out of `__libc_start_call_main` fails to unwind (caller pc reads as `0x101`) → "Cannot insert breakpoint 0" → GDB emits `*stopped` with no reason → a second finish aborts the phase. The engine now **continues** past no-reason stops and recovers any aborted execution command with one bounded continue (`trace.rs`). Verified: 12/12 bounded runs + full default runs all complete.
3. **rlimit mis-targeting**: the inferior's budget (incl. `RLIMIT_AS`) was applied to GDB, Valgrind and the ASan pass. ASan aborted instantly (`ReserveShadowMemoryRange failed… errno: 12`). GDB now runs unrestricted; tool children get CPU/FSIZE/NOFILE only (`resource_limits.rs`).

## Verified behavior

- **Acceptance**: `cargo run -- sample.c` → complete trace, exit 0, in ~5s: 26 snapshots (stepping through `main` → `__wrap_malloc` → `sum_of_three`), heap events (malloc 12 B + free), `heap_state` with raw bytes `0a000000140000001e000000` (10,20,30) and resolved call site `sample.c:30`, pointer own-address vs `points_to`, clean Valgrind report, exit code 0.
- **Crash path** (`null_deref.c`): `crashed` + SIGSEGV report with backtrace + ASan `SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: SEGV … in main` attached; Valgrind independently reports `InvalidRead`.
- **Limits** (`infinite_loop.c`, `many_allocs.c`): partial snapshots preserved, `limits_triggered` includes `max_steps`/`max_snapshot_count`, no orphaned inferior (GDB *and* inferior process groups now killed).
- **13 fixtures**: realloc chains, `calloc`, `allocation_failed`, leak, use-after-free, uninit, invalid write, big output, multi-TU project (steps across `main.c`/`helper.c`) all behave.
- **Exit codes**: 0 trace / 2 compile-failed (with precise SARIF line:col diagnostics — found and fixed a `startLine` camelCase bug) / 1 config error.

## Test suites

- **68 unit tests** green; **12 integration tests** green (19–38s, real gcc/gdb/valgrind, graceful skips with reasons on tool-less machines); `cargo clippy --all-targets` fully clean.
